commit 92fc204cf339b23c2ad3bc5ec69c65bdaf7a194e
Author:     John Bieling <john@thunderbird.net>
AuthorDate: Mon Jul 6 23:23:33 2026 +0000
Commit:     jtracey@thunderbird.net <jtracey@thunderbird.net>
CommitDate: Mon Jul 6 23:25:42 2026 +0000

    Bug 2017605 - Attempt to fix browser_weeklyUntil.js and browser_weeklyWithException.js by tolerating a trailing era marker in the calendar date-format probe. r=jtracey
    
    The intermittent "calendar-event-box ... did not appear in time" failure in
    recurrence/browser_weeklyUntil.js and browser_weeklyWithException.js was
    diagnosed from this macosx1015 opt run:
    https://treeherder.mozilla.org/jobs?repo=try-comm-central&revision=ff3dfe016d16390c3f9e3b3145293c50ca5f0fd9&selectedTaskRun=PS-qb_QNQEaweHPqezB0tQ.0
    
    On the CI workers where it fails, the OS short date format carries a trailing
    era marker (the narrow "A": "4/6/2002 A"). Why that marker is present on only
    some macOS runs is unknown - the resolved locale and calendar were identical
    ("en" / "gregory") on failing and passing workers, so the source of the extra
    era is not understood.
    
    `datetimepickers.js` probes the OS short date once per document scope by
    formatting a known date and matching it with a regex to learn the year/month/day
    order. The numeric regex allowed only a single optional trailing non-digit
    (`\D?`), so it failed to recognize the era-suffixed form; with the probe
    unrecognized, `parseDateTime()` returns null, the date typed into the recurrence
    dialog (the "until"/exception date) is never applied, the recurrence produces no
    occurrences, and the event box never renders.
    
    Forcing that era short date session-wide (via `intl.date_time.pattern_override`)
    reproduced the failure on Linux, Windows and macOS:
    https://treeherder.mozilla.org/jobs?repo=try-comm-central&revision=a756f304fcdef1165d89054596cf130ad9ffdf35
    
    With this fix applied on top of the same forced-era config, the tests pass on all
    platforms:
    https://treeherder.mozilla.org/jobs?repo=try-comm-central&revision=ff8c5a61d8d93c950409e664233dbd062b43333e
    
    Allow trailing non-digits (`\D*`) in the numeric date probe regex - matching the
    parse regex, which already tolerates a trailing suffix - so an era marker no
    longer defeats format detection.
    
    Differential Revision: https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D310611

diff --git a/calendar/base/content/widgets/datetimepickers.js b/calendar/base/content/widgets/datetimepickers.js
index 83293999725..0ad4ab0c11f 100644
--- a/calendar/base/content/widgets/datetimepickers.js
+++ b/calendar/base/content/widgets/datetimepickers.js
@@ -1322,7 +1322,9 @@
     // SHORT NUMERIC DATE, such as 2002-03-04, 4/3/2002, or CE2002Y03M04D.
     // Made of digits & nonDigits.  (Nondigits may be unicode letters
     // which do not match \w, esp. in CJK locales.)
-    parseShortDateRegex = /^\D*(\d+)\D+(\d+)\D+(\d+)\D?$/;
+    // Allow trailing non-digits (e.g. an era marker such as the narrow "A" that
+    // some locales' short date format now appends: "4/6/2002 A").
+    parseShortDateRegex = /^\D*(\d+)\D+(\d+)\D+(\d+)\D*$/;
     // Make sure to use UTC date and timezone here to avoid the pattern
     // detection to fail if the probe date output would have an timezone
     // offset due to our lack of support of historic timezone definitions.
title: Bug 2017605 - Attempt to fix browser_weeklyUntil.js and browser_weeklyWithException.js by tolerating a trailing era marker in the calendar date-format probe. r=jtracey
